title: Showing multiple volumes in a single volume rendering
abstract: ### Background One feature I've needed for a while is the ability to show multiple data cubes with different colormaps in a single volume rendering. I finally spent some time looking into this, and have come up with two solutions. I would like to contribute at least one of these to the VisPy code base (ideally both in the long run). Both approaches below apply to the additive volume rendering. ### Preview ### Approach 1 I modified the fragment shader for additive volume rendering to be able to include an arbitrary number of textures and corresponding colormaps: https://github.com/astrofrog/vispy-multivol/blob/master/multivol/multi_volume_shaders.py In the raytracing loop, I then average the colors from the different textures. I then created a `MultiVolumeVisual` class to which I can pass a list of tuples of `(data, clim, cmap)`, and the class deals with setting things up correctly: https://github.com/astrofrog/vispy-multivol/blob/master/multivol/multi_volume_visual.py ### Approach 2 I modified the fragment shader for additive volume rendering so that instead of using the colormap to get the color for a given texture value, I simply take the value of the texture itself: https://github.com/astrofrog/vispy-multivol/blob/master/multivol/rgba_volume_shaders.py I then created a `RGBAVolumeVisual` class that takes a 4d array with shape `(z, y, x, 4)` and then passes that directly to the texture. https://github.com/astrofrog/vispy-multivol/blob/master/multivol/rgba_volume_visual.py The data should be normalized before being passed to this class. So in this case, one can combine the multiple datasets/volumes by hand in Python using Numpy arrays, and pass the resulting array to the `RGBAVolume` class. ### Summary Both methods work well, and there are functional examples in the https://github.com/astrofrog/vispy-multivol repository and a screenshot at the top of this issue. Approach 2 could be implemented with minimal effort into VisPy - one simply need to check if the data passed is 4-d (I think this is already allowed) and if so, set a flag for the OpenGL code, then modify the `in_loop` code fragment to ignore the colormap if that flag is set. This could all be done in a dozen lines at the most. I could also add a `rgba_cube` boolean option in the `__init__` if needed. Would there be interest for me to open a pull request implementing approach 2? In the longer term, I think it would also be nice to have approach 1, because it allows the existing OpenGL colormaps to be used (whereas for approach 1, one has to have colormaps that can work in Python on Numpy arrays), so if there is interest, I can also open a pull request for this (for this one, I think it makes sense to create a separate `VolumeVisual` class rather than try and make `VolumeVisual` more complex. _For full code/description of the approaches with examples see here: https://github.com/astrofrog/vispy-multivol_
